newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt tightlipped on republic - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt tightlipped on republic - poll.

text.p: Almost 80 percent of Australian government members have refused to state an opinion on a whether Australia should become a republic, according to a newspaper poll published on Monday.
The Daily Telegraph newspaper found that 102 of the 129 Liberal-National coalition members refused to reveal their position on Australia becoming a republic.
Of the 28 government ministers, 24 refused to respond to the question, the survey found.

"It became clear during the survey that many coalition MPs (members of parliament) were not willing to risk alienating constituents -- or jeopardising their party preselection -- by divulging their position," the newspaper reported.
The survey found that only seven of the 104 Liberals were willing to declare that they supported a republic and only 14 that they were opposed.
Prime Minister John Howard, a well-known monarchist, did not respond definitively on the republic question, but his reply was counted as opposed.
"I do not believe that any republican system of government can deliver more stable and effective government than the present constitution," Howard said in response to the survey.
"In other words, I do not believe that the present system of government is flawed," he said.
In contrast to the government's reluctance, 73 of the 77 Labor Opposition members declared their support for a republic, none opposed a republic and four were non-committal.
